Doppler Width of an Emission Line

Source: R/doppler_width.R
doppler_width.Rd

Computes the full width at half maximum of the Doppler (thermal) broadening of a line emitted by atoms or ions of a given mass at a given temperature.

Usage

doppler_width(wavelength, temperature, mass)

Arguments

wavelength

The wavelength of the line, in nm.

temperature

The temperature of the emitters, in K.

mass

The mass of the emitter: its atomic mass, in u, or its element symbol (such as "Ca"), for the standard atomic weight.

Value

A numeric vector of Doppler widths (FWHM), in nm. The arguments are recycled to a common length.

Details

The thermal motion of the emitters gives a Gaussian profile of full width at half maximum $$w_D = \lambda \sqrt{\frac{8 k_B T \ln 2}{m c^2}}$$ where \(\lambda\) is the wavelength, \(T\) the temperature and \(m\) the mass of the emitter. In LIBS plasmas, it is usually much smaller than the instrumental width, except for light elements such as hydrogen. Both are Gaussian and add in quadrature, \(w_G = \sqrt{w_{inst}^2 + w_D^2}\), the Gaussian width to hold fixed in a Voigt fit (see peak_fit()).

See also

peak_fit(), voigt_fwhm()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

# Ca II 393.37 nm and H-alpha at 10000 K
doppler_width(c(393.37, 656.28), temperature = 10000, mass = c("Ca", "H"))
#> [1] 0.004450434 0.046818017

# with an instrumental width of 0.05 nm: the Gaussian width of a Voigt fit
sqrt(0.05^2 + doppler_width(393.37, 10000, "Ca")^2)
#> [1] 0.05019767
